findings.title: picocli.exit() will not compile
findings.body: The new code calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`, but the only picocli import in this file is `import picocli.CommandLine;`. `picocli` is a package, not a class, so there is no static `exit(int)` method to call and the expression does not resolve to anything. The code will fail to compile. The author most likely intended `System.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`, or to delegate back to the picocli CommandLine via `getCommandLine().get().setExecutionResult(...)` / throwing a `CommandLine.ParameterException`.

findings.title: picocli.exit() will not compile
findings.body: Same defect as in UpdateCompatibilityCheck: `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` is invoked, but the imports contain only `import picocli.CommandLine;`. `picocli` is a package name; there is no class named `picocli` with a static `exit` method to resolve. The new feature-disabled branch will not compile. Use `System.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` or the appropriate picocli mechanism (e.g. setting the CommandLine execution result).

findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changed from 4 to 3
findings.body: The constant `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from `4` to `3`, and `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` now occupies the old slot. Any automation (CI/CD scripts, GitOps pipelines) that was already treating exit code `4` as "recreate upgrade required" will silently misclassify that condition as "feature disabled" after this change. Even though the surrounding tool is preview, the documentation still presents the exit codes as a stable contract for automation and the change is undocumented in the diff. The new value `3` also collides conceptually with the standard "recreate / must shut down" message, which is fine semantically, yet the previous mapping was different. At minimum this should be called out as a breaking change to the preview contract, and ideally the doc in update-compatibility.adoc should explicitly note that exit code `4` previously meant recreate and now means feature disabled.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts message, not exit code 4
findings.body: The new `testFeatureNotEnabled` test verifies the user-facing error string but does not assert the exit code. The whole point of the new `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` constant and the matching doc table entry for exit code 4 is to give automation a reliable signal. The test should also `assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode())` (or the framework equivalent) so that a future regression where the command prints the message but returns a different exit code is caught.

findings.title: updatecompatibility macro hardcodes --features=rolling-updates
findings.body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now unconditionally appends ` --features=rolling-updates` to every rendered example, including usage that is meant to demonstrate the "feature not enabled" case (the very behavior asserted by `testFeatureNotEnabled`). Any documentation page that uses this macro will show users an example that explicitly turns the feature on, which makes it impossible to demonstrate the off-by-default behavior in docs. The macro should at most render the flag conditionally, or pages needing the negative example should be able to opt out.
